ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, rays $BA$ and $CA$ intersect at point $A$, with $BC$ connected. Given that $AB=AC$ and $\angle B=40^\circ$, what is the value of $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Since $AB = AC$ and $\angle B = 40^\circ$, it follows that $\angle C = \angle B = 40^\circ$, hence $x^\circ = 40^\circ + 40^\circ = \boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the attached figure, B is at the upper left, C is at the lower left, and BC forms a nearly vertical side; a line extending from B through A to the lower right intersects at A with a line extending from C through A to the upper right. The interior angle at B is marked as 40°, and the angle at the lower right of A is marked as x, belonging to the exterior angle at point A. Reasoning: the problem statement gives AB=AC, so triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, with base BC, hence the base angles ∠B and ∠C are equal. It is known that ∠B=40°, therefore ∠C=40°. According to the exterior angle theorem at point A, exterior angle x equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles, namely x=∠B+∠C=40°+40°=80°.
